en: Buddhavamsa 5.
The Buddha-chronicle of Maṅgala:
After Koṇḍañña, there was...
The leader named Maṅgala,
having destroyed darkness in the world,
upheld the vehicle of the Dhamma.
His radiance is incomparable,
surpassing that of all other Conquerors;
having eclipsed the light of the moon and the sun, it shines forth.
The ten-thousandfold world system shines forth.
That Buddha also proclaimed the four supreme, excellent truths.
Having drunk that essence of truth,
they dispel the great darkness;
having attained the incomparable enlightenment, they [liberate others].
During the first teaching of the Dhamma,
there was a realization of the Dhamma by one hundred thousand koṭis.
In the palace of Surindadeva,
the Buddha taught the Dhamma;
at that time, to thousands of millions—
The second occasion occurred when the wheel-turning monarch Sunanda approached the Perfectly Enlightened One.
Then the Fully Awakened One struck the most excellent drum of the Dhamma;
the people who were followers of Sunanda—
At that time there were nine hundred million;
all of them without exception became those who said, "Come, monk."
There were three assemblies for Maṅgala,
the Great Sage:
of one hundred thousand koṭis.
The first assembly was held;
the second consisted of one hundred thousand times ten million,
and the third of ninety million.
At that time there was a gathering of those whose taints were destroyed and who were stainless;
at that time, I was...
There was a brahmin named Suruci,
a reciter and a keeper of the mantras,
who had mastered the three Vedas.
Having approached him and gone for refuge to the Teacher,
I took refuge in the Saṅgha headed by the Perfectly Enlightened One.
I honored him with fragrant garlands;
having honored him with fragrant garlands,
I gratified him with milk for the cows.
That Buddha Maṅgala, the supreme among bipeds, also prophesied of me:
"In immeasurable eons..."
"This one will become a Buddha.
Having exerted himself in striving... [and so forth].
"May we be present before him.
Having heard her words as well,
my mind became even more serene.
I resolved upon a further vow for the fulfillment of the ten perfections; then,
increasing my joy, I—
For the sake of attaining the supreme enlightenment,
I gave my house to the Buddha and went forth into homelessness in his presence.
Having mastered the entire Suttanta and Vinaya—
the ninefold teaching of the Teacher— altogether,
I beautified the teaching of the Jina.
Dwelling there with diligence,
having cultivated the sublime meditation;
Having reached the perfection of direct knowledge,
I went to the Brahma-world.
There was a city named Uttara.
The kshatriya named Uttara was the father,
and the mother of the Great Seer Maṅgala was named Uttarā.
For nine thousand years he dwelt in the household life;
he was renowned, pure, and glorious.
There were three supreme palaces,
and thirty thousand women beautifully adorned.
A woman named Yasavatī and a son named Sīvala;
having seen four omens, [he departed].
He went forth by means of the horse Assaji;
for no less than eight months,
the Victor exerted himself in striving.
Being entreated by Brahmā,
the leader named Maṅgala,
the Great Hero, set the Wheel of Dhamma in motion.
In the most excellent forest Śrīvara,
Sudeva and Dhammasena were his chief disciples.
The attendant named Pālita of the great seer Maṅgala,
and Sīvalā and Asokā—
were his chief female disciples;
the Bodhi tree of that Blessed One is called the Nāga tree.
Nanda and Visākha were the foremost attendants;
Anulā and Sutanā likewise.
They were his foremost attendants.
Eighty thousand jewels rose up high,
towering above the Great Sage.
Then hundreds of thousands of rays stream forth;
for ninety thousand years,
As long as life remained,
for that long he stayed and delivered many people.
Just as the waves in the ocean cannot be counted,
even so his disciples [cannot be counted].
It is not possible to count them all,
until the Sambuddha Maṅgala, the Leader of the World, stood [in this world].
At that time, there was no death with defilements in his teaching.
Having upheld the foundation of the Dhamma,
Having delivered the great multitude of people, he,
of great renown, having blazed like a comet,
has gone out to extinction.
Having demonstrated the true nature of conditioned phenomena to the world with its devas,
and having blazed like a mass of fire, he has gone out.
Like the sun that has set,
the Buddha Maṅgala passed into Nibbāna in the rainy season retreat in the park.
“Right there his Jina-stūpa rose thirty yojanas high.
This is the third lineage of the Blessed One Maṅgala.
